title: Quantum MITM · pseudo-preimage

target.description: 9-round AES-192 compression pseudo-preimage with attacker-chosen IV and AES key/message. The figure has rounds0 through8, no final MixColumns, and terminal key addition.

setting.key_relation: The AES master-key input is chosen during public compression inversion; all round keys obey the standard schedule. No related secret keys or originally unknown master key are assumed.
setting.key_population: Attacker-controlled standard AES master-key input; no secret-key oracle
setting.plaintext_model: Jointly choose the 128-bit IV and complete standard AES message-key for one predetermined full128-bit output.
assumptions: QRAQM stores quantum states and supports unit-cost coherent random access. No physical implementation-resource estimate is included.
The standard AES key schedule is constrained; free key input is not independent arbitrary round keys.
Headline exponents omit constants in Theorem1 Eq8. The success guarantee uses the full theorem budget.

quantum_model.gate_set: Source-native reversible S-box or abstract quantum algorithm operations; no physical gate estimate.
quantum_model.routing: Physical routing is not part of this algorithmic estimate.
quantum_model.error_correction: Physical error correction is not part of this algorithmic estimate.
quantum_model.oracle_parallelism: The source total-work model is retained without additional parallel-oracle speedups.
quantum_model.solution_assumption: No unknown secret-key oracle. Coherent public compression evaluation and QRAQM table accesses; a single MITM solution and uniformly located solution episode/red element per Heuristic1.

time.note: Section2.2 quantum reduced-primitive operation model. Headline exponent suppresses constants; Eq8 supplies the conditional >=1/2 guarantee.

data.note: Offline public compression problem; no secret oracle data collection.

memory.note: Source Table1/Figure path memory; not bytes, encryption counts or physical qubits.

success.description: Theorem1 guarantees at least1/2 under a single uniformly located solution (Heuristic1), with its full Eq8 operation count and QRAQM. Section6 headline exponents suppress constants; this is not an exact 2^t-query finite-budget guarantee or original-key recovery. The source key-list notation and Eq10 have separate internal conflicts; the checked bound is conditional on the complete modeled algorithm, not a certified frontier vector.

review.scope: PDF pp.25–26 Section6.1/Figure10; pp.11–13 Theorem1/Heuristic1/Eqs8–11. Checked the theorem conditions against the displayed fixed path parameters.

evidence.interpretation: Defining primary-text costs, output event and conditions checked together.

limitations: The >=1/2 success guarantee is conditional on Heuristic1 and the full theorem cost, not on an exact headline operation count.

experiment.distinctness: One pseudo-preimage pair (h,m); both IV and message-key are free under the standard AES key schedule.
experiment.reference: Ideal 128-bit compression output with a fixed target; generic classical work 2^128 and quantum search 2^64. DM and MMO notation correspond by swapping the two free inputs.

field_conflicts.label: Printed Eq10 versus Eq8 and application time
field_conflicts.description: The simplified exponent in Eq10 adds min(lB,lR) to the search maximum. Expanding the full Eq8 combines those terms by a maximum instead. The Table1/Section6 headline is retained as a source claim; no corrected source edition is asserted.

observations.locator: PDF p.13 Eq10 and the fixed figure parameters.
observations.reported: Literal printed Eq10 gives exponent 84, unlike the full Eq8 or the application headline.

field_conflicts.label: Pre-cancel versus post-cancel key-list notation
field_conflicts.description: PDF9 defines |KB|/|KR| as valid post-cancel lists. Eqs8–9 then divide them by cancellation factors again. The application text instead uses Grover search over the pre-cancel key domain. Setup is retained in the full algorithm work; the inconsistent notation is not silently treated as a speedup.

observations.reported: Theorem preparation terms divide by cancellation factors; application schedules use pre-cancel search domains.
